dataset.description:
The AFLACHECK research initiative adopts a comprehensive, interdisciplinary approach to assess and manage the risks of aflatoxin (AFs) contamination in the dairy supply chain, with the aim of ensuring safe and healthy products from farm to table.
The project is based on the generation, integration, and analysis of large and heterogeneous datasets related to AFs contamination at different stages of the dairy production chain. These include data on feed contamination, animal exposure, carry-over processes, milk contamination levels, and human exposure. By applying artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) techniques, these datasets will be used to identify trends, detect anomalies, and predict contamination risks.
The purpose of this data-driven approach is to support the development of a decision-support system that enables proactive, risk-based monitoring and early warning, moving beyond traditional reactive testing. Effective data management is essential to ensure data quality, consistency, traceability, and interoperability across all project phases, as well as to facilitate data sharing and reuse in line with open science and FAIR principles.
This approach contributes to improved food safety management systems, supports evidence-based regulatory decision-making, and enhances the efficiency and sustainability of monitoring practices in the dairy sector.

distribution.title:
The purpose of data collection and generation in the AFLACHECK project is to support the development of predictive models, risk-based monitoring strategies, and early warning systems for aflatoxin contamination in the dairy supply chain. The collected data will enable the assessment of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) occurrence in feed, estimation of carry-over rates to aflatoxin M1 (AFM1) in milk, evaluation of animal-related factors, and modeling of human exposure.
These datasets directly contribute to the project objectives by enabling evidence-based risk assessment, improving early detection of contamination, and supporting decision-making in food safety management.
The data originate from both primary and secondary sources. Primary data include longitudinal sampling and laboratory analyses of feed and milk (e.g., ELISA and confirmatory LC-MS/MS), animal welfare assessments based on physiological and production indicators, and dietary intake data collected through food consumption surveys (FFQ and 24-hour recall). Secondary data include historical contamination data from monitoring programs and relevant environmental or climate data from open-access sources.

dmp.description:
The AFLACHECK project aims to develop a simulation-based self-control and early warning system to prevent and manage aflatoxin M1 (AFM1) contamination in milk by integrating predictive modeling, risk-based monitoring, and real-time data analysis.
The project adopts a comprehensive farm-to-fork approach, generating and integrating multiple types of data, including aflatoxin contamination in feed, carry-over rates from feed to milk, animal health and welfare parameters, milk contamination levels, and human exposure data. These datasets will support the development of artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI-ML) models for predicting AFM1 occurrence and enabling risk ranking and prioritization across the dairy supply chain.
AFLACHECK focuses on reducing human exposure to aflatoxins, improving animal health and welfare, and supporting evidence-based decision-making in food safety management systems. The project will produce analytical, modeling, and survey data, as well as software tools and decision-support systems, ensuring their proper management, accessibility, and reuse in accordance with FAIR principles.
dmp.ethical_issues_description:
Yes, certain ethical and legal considerations may impact data collection and sharing within the AFLACHECK project. These primarily relate to the handling of potentially sensitive information, such as data collected from dairy farms, as well as human-related data obtained through dietary surveys.
All data collection activities will be conducted in compliance with applicable legal and ethical frameworks, including data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR) and relevant institutional guidelines. Personal and sensitive data will be anonymized or pseudonymized prior to storage and sharing.
Informed consent will be obtained from participants involved in surveys, and any data related to farms or stakeholders will be handled with strict confidentiality and, where necessary, shared under controlled access conditions.
Animal-related data will be collected in accordance with established animal welfare standards and ethical research practices.

project.description: The AFLACHECK project aims to develop a predictive risk-based system for aflatoxin M1 contamination in milk using digital early warning tools, machine learning models, and optimized feed formulation strategies. The project is funded by the Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia under the IDEJA programme and coordinated by the Institute of Meat Hygiene and Technology.
